references.text: Reiterates the prohibition against sexual relations with a father's wife and establishes the death penalty as the consequence for this sin.
Prohibits a man from taking his father's wife, thereby dishonoring his father, using the same expression of 'uncovering his father's nakedness'.
Declares a curse upon anyone who lies with his father's wife because he uncovers his father's nakedness.
Reuben lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, an example of violating this prohibition.
Jacob mentions Reuben's sin with his concubine as the reason Reuben loses his birthright.
Absalom publicly lay with his father's concubines, a serious violation of this commandment.
Adonijah requests Abishag, David's young wife, which Solomon interprets as a grave offense.
Ezekiel accuses Israel of dishonoring their father's nakedness, directly referencing this prohibition.
Paul rebukes the church in Corinth because a man is living with his father's wife, a sin even pagans condemn.
